key_insight: MP-Bench introduces a benchmark for evaluating voice agents in realistic multi-party conversations, going beyond standard one-on-one tests. It helps reveal how well an agent can handle turn-taking, speaker tracking, and participation in more complex social settings.
problem_solved: Existing voice-agent benchmarks focus mostly on dyadic interactions or passive audio understanding, leaving a major gap in evaluating performance in multi-party conversations. This paper addresses the difficulty of measuring agent behavior in settings where multiple speakers create exponentially more complex conversational dynamics.
method: Design a benchmark specifically for multi-party conversation participation by voice agents.
Evaluate agents on interaction skills that matter in group settings, such as identifying when to speak, following conversation flow, and responding appropriately amid multiple speakers.
Use benchmark tasks to compare systems under realistic conversational conditions that are harder than standard one-on-one evaluation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MP-Bench provides a more realistic yardstick for building and testing voice agents intended for real-world use. It can expose failures that traditional benchmarks miss, guiding better model design and deployment decisions.
visual_elements: A side-by-side diagram comparing dyadic vs. multi-party conversation evaluation.
A conversation flow graphic showing multiple speakers and the agent’s turn-taking decisions.
A benchmark scorecard with metrics for speaker tracking, timing, and response quality.
An icon set representing voice, multiple users, and dialogue turns.
paper_title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant
paper_authors: Yi-Jen Shih, Shih-Yun Shan Kuan, Guan-Ting Lin, Kai-Wei Chang, Siddhant Arora
